187	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:

191	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
192	        """List one directory of the checkout: one entry per line as kind, size, name. Path is the
193	        directory to list, relative to the checkout root; '.' is the root.
194	
195	        Args:
196	            path: The directory to list, relative to the checkout root.
197	        """
198	        try:
199	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
200	            if not p.is_dir():
201	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
202	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
203	            skip = self.hidden if rel == "." else (".git",)  # git's own files are never listed
204	            entries = [e for e in entries if e.name not in skip]
205	            lines = []
206	            for e in entries[:LIST_CAP]:
207	                kind = "link" if e.is_symlink() else "dir" if e.is_dir() else "file"
208	                size = e.lstat().st_size if kind == "file" else 0
209	                name = e.name if rel == "." else f"{rel}/{e.name}"  # paths from the checkout root
210	                lines.append(f"{kind}\t{size}\t{name}")
211	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:
212	                lines.append(f"...\t{len(entries) - LIST_CAP} more entries not shown")
213	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
214	            return f"error: {e}"
215	        self.listed.append(rel)
216	        return "\n".join(lines) or "(empty)"

218	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
219	        """Read a file of the checkout as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
220	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
221	
222	        Args:
223	            path: The file to read, relative to the checkout root.
224	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
225	        """
226	        try:
227	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
228	            if not p.is_file():
229	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
230	            start = max(1, int(start))
231	            out: list[str] = []
232	            n = nbytes = 0
233	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
234	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
235	                    if i < start:
236	                        continue
237	                    size = len(line.encode())
238	                    if n >= READ_LINES_CAP or nbytes + size > READ_BYTES_CAP:
239	                        if n:  # one line per call at least, or a long line dead-ends the read
240	                            out.append(f"...\ttruncated; continue with start={i}")
241	                            break
242	                        cut = line.encode()[:READ_BYTES_CAP].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
243	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{cut} …(line cut at {READ_BYTES_CAP} bytes)")
244	                    else:
245	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{line.rstrip(chr(10))}")
246	                    n += 1
247	                    nbytes += size
248	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
249	            return f"error: {e}"
250	        self.read_paths.append(rel)
251	        self.lines_read += n
252	        return "\n".join(out) or "(empty)"

254	    def _files(self, directory: Path, rel: str, unlistable: list[int]):
255	        """Every file under `directory`, in the order `list` gives: directories first, then files,
256	        each by name, hidden names at the root and any .git component skipped, symlinks not
257	        followed. Yields the file and its path from the checkout root. A directory that cannot be
258	        listed appends 1 to `unlistable`: what is under it was not searched."""
259	        try:
260	            entries = sorted(directory.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
261	        except (OSError, RuntimeError):  # a directory that cannot be listed: nothing under it
262	            unlistable.append(1)
263	            return
264	        for e in entries:
265	            if e.is_symlink():  # a link is not a file of the checkout, whatever it points at
266	                continue
267	            if e.name == ".git" or (rel == "." and e.name in self.hidden):
268	                continue
269	            child = e.name if rel == "." else f"{rel}/{e.name}"
270	            if e.is_dir():
271	                yield from self._files(e, child, unlistable)
272	            elif e.is_file():
273	                yield e, child

275	    def search(self, pattern: str, path: str = ".") -> str:
276	        """Search the checkout for a pattern: every line of every file under `path` that contains
277	        `pattern` as plain text, case-sensitive, one match per line as `<path>:<line number>:<text>`.
278	        Files come in the order `list` gives and lines in order, numbered as `read` numbers them; at
279	        most 100 lines or 32000 bytes per search, then how many more matches were not shown. A file
280	        whose bytes are not UTF-8, one larger than 1000000 bytes, or one that cannot be read is
281	        skipped, and the result ends with how many files that was. A lone match longer than the cap
282	        is cut to fit and marked, as `read` cuts a long line.
283	
284	        Args:
285	            pattern: The plain text to find; case-sensitive, and must not be empty or have a newline
286	                in it.
287	            path: The directory to search, relative to the checkout root; '.' is the root.
288	        """
289	        if not pattern:
290	            return "error: the pattern is empty"
291	        if "\n" in pattern or "\r" in pattern:
292	            return "error: the pattern has a newline; search matches one line at a time"
293	        try:
294	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
295	            if not p.is_dir():
296	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
297	            out: list[str] = []
298	            shown = nbytes = total = skipped = 0
299	            unlistable: list[int] = []
300	            full = False  # the first match that does not fit ends the shown part
301	            for f, frel in self._files(p, rel, unlistable):
302	                try:
303	                    if f.stat().st_size > SEARCH_FILE_CAP:  # too large: never opened
304	                        skipped += 1
305	                        continue
306	                    with f.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:  # line by line, universal newlines
307	                        hits = [(i, line.rstrip("\n")) for i, line in enumerate(fh, 1) if pattern in line]
308	                except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):  # not UTF-8, or unreadable: the file is skipped
309	                    skipped += 1
310	                    continue
311	                for i, line in hits:
312	                    total += 1
313	                    if full or shown >= SEARCH_LINES_CAP:
314	                        continue
315	                    entry = f"{frel}:{i}:{line}"
316	                    size = len(entry.encode()) + 1
317	                    if nbytes + size > SEARCH_BYTES_CAP:
318	                        full = True
319	                        if not shown:  # one match longer than the cap: cut it and mark it, as read does
320	                            head = f"{frel}:{i}:"
321	                            marker = f" …(match cut at {SEARCH_BYTES_CAP} bytes)"
322	                            room = SEARCH_BYTES_CAP - len((head + marker).encode())
323	                            cut = line.encode()[: max(0, room)].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
324	                            out.append(head + cut + marker)
325	                            shown += 1
326	                        continue
327	                    out.append(entry)
328	                    nbytes += size
329	                    shown += 1
330	            skipped += len(unlistable)  # a directory that could not be listed counts once
331	            if not total:
332	                found = "no matches"
333	            else:
334	                found = "\n".join(out)
335	                if total > shown:
336	                    found += f"\n...\t{total - shown} more matches not shown"
337	            if skipped:
338	                found += f"\n...\t{skipped} files not searched"
339	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
340	            return f"error: {e}"
341	        self.searched.append(rel)
342	        return found

347	
348	        Args:
349	            path: The file to write, relative to the checkout root.

351	        """

353	        if capped:
354	            return capped
355	        try:
356	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
357	            self._writable(rel)
358	            p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

365	    def edit(self, path: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:
366	        """Edit a file of the checkout: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
367	        file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
368	        tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.
369	
370	        Args:
371	            path: The file to edit, relative to the checkout root.
372	            old: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.
373	            new: The text to put in its place.
374	        """
375	        capped = self._capped()
376	        if capped:
377	            return capped
378	        if not old:  # every file contains the empty string, everywhere
379	            return "error: old text is empty"
380	        try:
381	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
382	            self._writable(rel)
383	            if not p.is_file():
384	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
385	            text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
386	            found = text.count(old)
387	            if found != 1:
388	                if found == 0:
389	                    return f"error: old text not found in {rel}"
390	                return f"error: old text found {found} times in {rel}; include more context"
391	            before = len(text.splitlines())
392	            text = text.replace(old, new, 1)
393	            p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
394	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError
395	            return f"error: {e}"
396	        self.edited.append(rel)
397	        return f"edited {rel} ({before} -> {len(text.splitlines())} lines)"

399	    def check(self) -> str:
400	        """Run the checkout's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
401	        green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the checkout read-only and
402	        no network, so this reports on the checkout as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.
403	        """
404	        if len(self.checks) >= CHECK_CAP:
405	            return f"error: cap reached ({CHECK_CAP} checks); report now"
406	        if self.sandbox is None:
407	            return "error: no sandbox; check is not available in this run"
408	        n = len(self.checks) + 1
409	        t0 = time.time()
410	        try:
411	            code, output = self.sandbox.run(self.root, self.run_dir, n)
412	            seconds = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
413	            log = self.run_dir / f"check-{n}.log"
414	            log.write_text(output, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
415	        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
416	            return f"error: {e}"
417	        self.checks.append({"exit": code, "seconds": seconds})
418	        tail = "\n".join(output.splitlines()[-CHECK_TAIL_LINES:])
419	        if len(tail.encode()) > CHECK_TAIL_BYTES:  # the end of the output is the part that says why
420	            tail = tail.encode()[-CHECK_TAIL_BYTES:].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
421	        return f"exit {code}\n{tail}"
